# Test fixtures

No Navimow account was available: these answers are shaped after the code
that reads the real ones, except the error answers, which are real.

| File                                                           | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid-grant.json`, `token-empty.json`, `oauth-illegal.json` | **Real answers**, probed on 2026-10-16 without an account: the token endpoint (HTTP 400) for an unknown code or refresh token, `authList` (HTTP 200) without a token and with a refused one (`getVehicleStatus` and `mqtt/userInfo/get/v2` answer the same).                                                                    |
| `token.json`, `token-refreshed.json`                           | The standard OAuth2 answer the token endpoint gives Home Assistant's `LocalOAuth2Implementation` (NavimowHA `auth.py`) and ioBroker.navimow (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expires_in`); made-up values.                                                                                                                    |
| `devices.json`                                                 | `GET /openapi/smarthome/authList` as navimow-sdk 0.1.2 reads it (`api.py` `async_get_devices`, `models.py` `Device.from_dict`: `data.payload.devices[]` with `id`, `name`, `model`, `firmware_version`, `serial_number`, `online`, `productKey`, `deviceName`, `iotId`); made-up mowers, the second one with an id to sanitize. |
| `statuses.json`                                                | `POST /openapi/smarthome/getVehicleStatus` as navimow-sdk reads it (`DeviceStatus.from_dict`: `vehicleState`, `capacityRemaining[].rawValue/unit`, `descriptiveCapacityRemaining`, `error_code`) and ioBroker.navimow (`updateDevices`, the battery from `capacityRemaining`); the vehicle states are the ones ioBroker lists.  |
| `commands-*.json`                                              | `POST /openapi/smarthome/sendCommands` as navimow-sdk reads it (`async_send_command`: `data.payload.commands[]` with `status` and `errorCode`, `alreadyInState` counted as a success).                                                                                                                                          |
| `mqtt-info.json`                                               | `GET /openapi/mqtt/userInfo/get/v2` as NavimowHA and ioBroker.navimow read it (`mqttHost`, `mqttUrl`, `userName`, `pwdInfo`); made-up broker and credentials.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `mqtt-state.json`                                              | Messages of the `state` channel: `{ "state": "isRunning", "battery": 79 }` is the one NavimowHA's tests push (`tests/test_state_freshness.py`), `{ "battery": 81 }` the one of ioBroker.navimow's tests; the `error` object follows navimow-sdk's `DeviceStateMessage` (`error: { code, message }`).                            |
| `location.json`                                                | `start`, `firstPercent`, `sessionDone` and `lateArrival` are **real readings** of a Navimow, recorded by ioBroker.navimow (`main.test.js`, MIT, 2026-08-11) from the debug log of a real mower; `posture` follows the posture readings of the same file (positions are not used by this integration).                           |
